views.markdown: A different terminal to use. diffTerm runs a real shell on your jailbroken iPhone or iPad and draws it the way a terminal is supposed to be drawn, so the tools you already use behave the way you expect.

When iOS reclaims diffTerm in the background, each tab's screen is saved on the way out and put back the next time you open it, under a line saying the earlier processes are gone, so old output is never mistaken for a live shell.

Written from scratch against the DEC VT500 state diagram rather than by pattern-matching escape sequences: VT100, VT220 and xterm controls, 24-bit colour, the alternate screen, scroll regions, mouse reporting (X10 through SGR), synchronized updates, Sixel graphics and iTerm2 inline images (`imgcat`). Accuracy is measured with esctest.

views.title: Knows where commands begin and end

views.markdown: Shell integration marks (OSC 133) turn your scrollback into command blocks: tap to copy one command's output, jump between prompts, see exit codes and how long things took. Fish and zsh integrations ship in the bundle.

- A jailbroken iPhone or iPad on iOS 14 or later, arm64.
- Rootless (Dopamine, palera1n), roothide (Serotonin with Bootstrap, Relaxin) or rootful (palera1n in rootful mode). Your package manager picks the matching package.
- Nothing else: everything it needs ships in the package.

The iPad layout is implemented but has not been run on real hardware.
**Sessions.** Shells run inside the app and end with it: closing a tab stops its shell, and so does iOS reclaiming the app.
**Updates.** Builds publish automatically from the source repository. Every version stays downloadable here, so rolling back is a normal package-manager operation.

- Keyboard opens faster.
- Three-finger copy and paste.
- Copy after Select All.
- bash no longer crashes on locales iOS lacks (en_US.UTF-8, C.UTF-8).
